Rule #0 for any service I open to the world (like my Minecraft server) is DON'T MAKE UNENFORCEABLE RULES. Any rule that is stated and then not enforced erodes the respect and trust of the user base that any rules will be enforced at all.

If you have a "one account per person" rule, but you can't identify individuals coming from VPNs and proxies, then there are two options: (1) eliminate the one account rule for everyone, or (2) throttle usage by VPN and proxy users so that they can't do large amounts of damage. I would go so far as to forbid account creation over a VPN or proxy. (You can use one that already exists, but not make new ones.) Unfortunately, this doesn't work with the "one account per IP" method either. There are far too many ways to access the site from multiple IP addresses, and too many situations of legitimately different users getting NATted onto the same IP.

In the case of the Minecraft server, I have the benefit of knowing that new accounts cost money. I've had to deal with banned players coming back with alts to do damage, but it's rare. In one of those cases, I banned the IP range of the entire school, and ended up locking out one of my own admins that went to that same school. He resolved the issue by tracking down and beating the crap out of the guy who had griefed the server twice, at which point I lifted the ban and never had a problem from there again.

I had plenty of cases of siblings (or even parent and child, like my co-owner and his son) both playing on my server from the same location, often at the same time, so I never expected unique IP addresses per player. I suppose it's a bit different with a game, where people will be inclined to jump on from the same room at the same time specifically because they are in the same room. I didn't ban alts either, as long as they weren't being used to unbalance the game. (After all, you can only physically handle one set of inputs at a time, and I have alts myself, though I play them as completely independent entities.) The server still exists, but the player base and utilization are both WAY down from what they used to be.
